unmapped_findings: The processing temperature window for 15Mn5Ni alloy was found to be around 1173 K; upon heat treatment at 973 K and 1023 K this alloy displayed very low ductility (<1%), attributed to the presence of a large volume fraction of B2 particles and co-precipitation of coarser κ-carbides and B2 along grain boundaries.
Volume fraction of B2 particles in 15Mn5Ni decreased drastically from ~40% at 973 K to ~15% at 1173 K, whereas in hot rolled condition the prior B2 fraction was ~12%.

XRD of 15Mn5Ni after heat treatment at 973 K showed additional peaks corresponding to κ-carbides and B2 relative to the cold rolled condition, and the B2 diffraction peaks were more intense at 973 K than at 1173 K, indicating a higher volume fraction of secondary phases at lower annealing temperature.

Bulk Vickers hardness of 15Mn5Ni in the HR+CR+973 K condition is not reported numerically; the Ni-containing alloys (28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni) had significantly higher hardness than the 28Mn0Ni alloy at any given heat-treatment temperature and their hardness decreased monotonically with increasing heat-treatment temperature, increasing to ~500 VHN upon heat treatment at 873 K.

TEM-EDS composition of the B2 phase in 15Mn5Ni was reported only for the 1173 K condition (Mn 10.5–8.7 wt.%, Al 12.8–13.5 wt.%, Ni 20.2–22.0 wt.%; correspondingly Mn 9.5–7.8 at.%, Al 23.5–24.6 at.%, Ni 17.0–18.5 at.%), and not for the 973 K condition; the B2 phase was identified as an FeAl based phase containing significant Mn and Ni.

A prominent coarser B2 precipitate-rich zone formed around deformed austenite in 15Mn5Ni alloy during heat treatment at 973 K, whereas in 28Mn5Ni fine secondary B2 was precipitated mostly along grain boundaries.
The size of κ-carbides in deformed austenite regions of 15Mn5Ni was higher than in 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni alloys under the same 973 K heat-treatment condition.

All three alloys (including 15Mn5Ni) attained similar strength levels (~450 VHN hardness) after 50% cold reduction; the strength of 50% cold rolled alloys increased to ~1.4–1.8 GPa at the expense of ductility.

At the HR+CR (50% cold reduction) condition 15Mn5Ni exhibited YS 1665 ± 12 MPa, UTS 1800 ± 15 MPa and total elongation 7 ± 0.5% (this is the precursor cold-rolled state, not the 973 K heat-treated state of this sample).
